programme: Two linked developmental progenitor-identity modules: SALL4, UTF1, ID4 and ZNF281 form a pluripotency/stemness circuit built around NANOG (SALL4 and ZNF281 both target NANOG; SALL4 also targets SOX2, EPCAM, ABCG2, CD44-family stem markers; UTF1 is itself defined as an undifferentiated-embryonic-cell factor; ID4 blocks differentiation via BRCA1/TP53/SOX2/MBP repression). Separately, ISL1 and LHX3 are the classical LIM-homeodomain pair that specifies motor-neuron identity during development, with EN1 contributing a Wnt/Shh-driven midbrain-hindbrain patterning axis (its targets WNT1, GLI3, FGF8, CTNNB1 are the textbook En1-Wnt1-Fgf8-Gli3 organizer set).
role_in_a: In breast cancer the SALL4-UTF1-ID4-ZNF281 module reactivates an embryonic stem/progenitor transcriptional state that blocks luminal differentiation and sustains a basal-like, immune-evasive, therapy-resistant triple-negative phenotype; this is the best-supported arm, with direct papers for SALL4, UTF1 and ID4 individually in breast cancer.
role_in_b: In the neural tissue relevant to stroke, ISL1 and LHX3 acting as the LIM-homeodomain motor-neuron specification pair, together with EN1's midbrain/cerebellar patterning role, push injured or reprogrammed neurons back toward an immature, developmentally 'younger' transcriptional state — a manoeuvre shown (PMID 40796666, shared by ISL1 and LHX3) to suppress neurodegenerative pathology when used therapeutically, and consistent with EN1's documented role in cerebellar output-neuron survival.
shared_axis: Both diseases redeploy lineage-appropriate developmental 'master' progenitor-identity transcription factors to push a committed cell back toward a progenitor-like, plasticity-permissive state — pluripotency factors doing this in the tumor to sustain stemness and resistance, LIM-homeodomain neuronal-identity factors doing it in the injured CNS to attempt survival or repair. No single paper states this connection; it follows from the fact that dedifferentiation-toward-progenitor-state is separately established as a mechanism in each disease.
reasoning: The module is nameable and several factors are independently placed in breast cancer (SALL4, UTF1, ID4) or in progenitor/motor-neuron biology relevant to CNS injury (ISL1, LHX3, EN1), but no retrieved paper puts any factor in both diseases at once, so the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about shared developmental logic rather than a documented fact. ZNF281 has only a weak, single stroke-adjacent hit and no breast-cancer paper despite a favorable Open Targets score, which caps confidence rather than raising it.
support: PMID 41498967, 41925953, 41886924, 40890202 — SALL4 in breast cancer (PD-L1/immune evasion, biomarker roles); PMID 38850245, 35631536, 33718351 — SALL4 in spinal cord identity, ischemic stroke models, and cardiac reprogramming after injury; PMID 36760370, 25435811 — UTF1 expression and significance in breast cancer; PMID 40640173, 40186425 — ID4 as a TNBC driver and mammary-development regulator; PMID 36172261 — ZNF281 as an immune biomarker in subarachnoid hemorrhage; PMID 42099237, 29497310 — ISL1 promoting breast cancer proliferation/invasion; PMID 41883246, 40614918, 42425092, 40796666 — ISL1 in neural progenitor, ferroptosis-protective, and motor-neuron-programming contexts; PMID 40796666, 36109497, 35177643, 32783653 — LHX3 in motor neuron maturation and generation; PMID 40207200 — EN1 noted in a breast cancer transcriptome context; PMID 39984491, 38912572 — EN1 in cerebellar neuron development and survival.
how_to_falsify: In a TNBC stem-cell/organoid model, knock down SALL4, ID4 and ZNF281 together and check whether the NANOG/SOX2-centered stemness signature and basal identity collapse; in parallel, in a post-ischemic neuron or reprogramming model, knock down ISL1 and LHX3 together and check whether the immature/motor-neuron-like gene reactivation seen in PMID 40796666 fails to occur. If either module's signature is unaffected by removing its named factors, or if ChIP-seq shows SALL4/ZNF281 do not actually co-bind NANOG-proximal elements in the breast tumor cells, or ISL1/LHX3 do not co-occupy the same LIM-homeodomain motor-neuron enhancers in the stroke-relevant cells, the proposed module-and-reactivation account is wrong.
caveats: The tissue pairing is blood (stroke side) versus breast (tumor side), so the neural roles claimed for ISL1, LHX3 and EN1 are read from brain-development and motor-neuron/ALS literature, not from the blood expression data that actually generated the stroke network edges — this is an inferential leap, not a tissue-matched finding. Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 117 patient-group comparisons, so the 51-71/117 support fractions reflect a modest number of truly independent replicates. SALL4 is flagged discordant rather than concordant, meaning its target-set agreement runs in the opposite direction between the two diseases, so if it belongs to this module the two diseases likely engage it with opposite polarity, not the same one. UTF1 and ID4 have no stroke-side literature at all, so their part in role_in_b is extrapolated from the logic of the module rather than independently placed. ASH1L, ZFP64, NCOA4, SIM2 and TCFL5 were excluded from the account: NCOA4's network targets (AR, KLK3, TFF1) point to a nuclear-receptor-coactivator role, but the only literature retrieved for it concerns a different function (ferritinophagy/ferroptosis), so building on it would conflate two distinct NCOA4 biologies; the others returned no usable disease-specific evidence. Generic immune/tissue factors (STAT1, IRF4, CEBPB, SPI1, etc.) were already removed as tissue-generic, so this account is deliberately about developmental identity factors rather than shared inflammation.
